Team — quick proposal based on AP’s preference and our typical finance constraints. Options with pros/cons: 

Option A — Separate invoices per ClearSpring legal entity (recommended if AP requires it):
- We issue one invoice per Redwood billing/legal entity that maps to the purchasing entity on the PO.
- Each invoice contains full legal name, VAT/Tax registration, bank details, and a distinct invoice number (e.g., RWI-US-20261110-001).
- Pros: Easy for AP to match and pay; simpler VAT treatment per jurisdiction.
- Cons: More work to create multiple invoices; must ensure PO/line splitting is precise.

Option B — Single consolidated invoice with entity allocation sections:
- One PDF invoice with separate sections per purchasing entity. Each section has its own subtotal and designation to a legal entity. Also include a combined remittance advice page.
- Pros: Single file for contract; lower invoicing overhead for us.
- Cons: Some AP systems balk at single invoice with multiple 'invoices' embedded; reconciliation friction.

Recommendation: Default to Option A when ClearSpring AP says they need separate invoices. We should template the invoice to include: ClearSpring PO number, PO line references, cost-center tags (provided by ClearSpring), and a per-line mapping field (ledger_tag) so Marissa’s team can auto-route.

Also: for EU VAT — please confirm ClearSpring Europe GmbH’s VAT number and whether they will self-account under reverse charge. If they are reverse charge, we will omit VAT and include the wording required by local tax law.

I attached a sample (split_invoice_sample.pdf) showing the formatting we usually send to enterprise APs.

-Karthik
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Marissa / team — a few finance constraints and required fields for AP compliance: 

1) Invoice level requirements per entity (must include):
   - Redwood legal entity name + registered address + VAT/Tax ID (if applicable)
   - Unique invoice number and invoice date
   - Clear mapping to the PO (PO_7890 and PO line references)
   - Bank account and remittance instructions for the receiving entity; we cannot mix bank accounts across entities on the same invoice.

2) VAT treatment:
   - If ClearSpring Europe GmbH confirms reverse-charge, we will provide a 0% VAT invoice with the required reverse-charge text and our EU VAT number.
   - If not reverse-charge, VAT will be charged according to the selling entity’s jurisdiction; we’ll need to confirm tax registration for the entity that will be invoicing.

3) Suggested invoice numbering convention to reduce duplication: RWI-<ENTITY>-YYYYMMDD-<seq>. Example: RWI-EU-20261110-01

4) For payments: AP prefers separate remittance advices. We can provide a consolidated remittance advice PDF that lists all entity invoices and the associated bank details to help their Treasury team.

Action for us: Marissa to build the invoices once we have cost center codes and confirmed VAT status. I’ll attach our remittance instruction sheet for each entity (remittance_instructions.pdf).

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Finance — Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
